To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
laminin-1 is involved in epithelial branching morphogenesis and that this effect is mediated by dystroglycan.
laminins are crucial for branching morphogenesis and that laminin binding to dystroglycan is important for this process.
laminin-1 interacts with dystroglycan, a component of the dystrophin glycoprotein complex, to regulate the branching morphogenesis of the kidney, lung and submandibular salivary gland.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate epithelial morphogenesis and how this knowledge can be used to develop new therapeutic strategies for diseases that affect organogenesis.
the identification of the laminin-binding cell surface molecules that regulate branching morphogenesis and the role of these molecules in branching morphogenesis.
the identification and characterization of cell surface molecules that interact with the basement membrane components and regulate branching morphogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
laminin-1, together with its cell surface receptors, is a key molecule in branching morphogenesis.
laminin-1 is a major component of the basement membrane and is involved in the regulation of branching morphogenesis of several epithelia.
the laminin-1/laminin-10/laminin-11/laminin-8 family is a major regulator of epithelial morphogenetic events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the laminin-binding integrins and dystroglycan are involved in the control of branching morphogenesis in these tissues.
the laminin-1/laminin-2 complex, through interactions with the dystroglycan complex, plays a role in epithelial morphogenesis by modulating cell shape and motility.
laminin-1 is a critical regulator of branching morphogenesis in the developing salivary gland and lung.
The main takeaway from our work is that

laminins, in association with dystroglycan, may play a role in the branching morphogenesis of epithelia by controlling the organization of the extracellular matrix and the cell surface, and by modulating the activity of the cell surface receptor tyrosine kinases, such as the hepatocyte growth factor receptor (MET).
the laminin-binding protein dystroglycan is involved in epithelial branching morphogenesis.
laminins and dystroglycan are involved in the branching morphogenesis of several organs.
